cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic evaluates whether the current two-set membership is coherently represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The two sets are of comparable size (55 and 48) and show nearly identical mean within-set affinity (0.00929 and 0.00936), indicating similar internal cohesion. The between-set affinity (0.00902) is only slightly lower than either within-set value, so the current pair boundary is weakly expressed in fused affinity terms rather than sharply separated. The eigengap profiles for both sets are dominated by the k=1 resolution (leading gaps 0.328 and 0.301), with all higher-resolution gaps falling to the 10^-3 to 10^-4 range; the screening therefore resolves to candidate_k=1 for both sets. Taken together, the measurements describe a partition whose two memberships are internally comparable and whose boundary is modest in fused geometry, while the partition-level screening does not surface a dominant internal subdivision signal. These are structural descriptions of the current partition, not conclusions about whether the partition should be retained, split, or merged.

The CT silhouette is near zero, indicating essentially no separation of the current labels in CT distance space, while the other three modalities show small positive separation. Global patient-geometry similarity (GRV) is highest between WSI and RNA (0.198, permutation p=0.001), followed by CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001) and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001); these pairs share more global patient geometry than expected under exchangeable correspondence. CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096) show lower GRV with nonsignificant permutation p-values. The pattern indicates that the four views are not uniformly concordant: the RNA, WSI, and WXS views share moderate global geometry with each other, while CT is the least concordant with the molecular views. Importantly, high GRV does not establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and low GRV can reflect complementary information rather than a faulty modality. The weak native-distance silhouettes indicate that the current pair boundary is not sharply expressed in any single view, consistent with the weakly expressed boundary described in the prior structural report.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics described comparable internal cohesion of the two sets and a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry, with partition-level eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The GRV results add a cross-view geometry comparison that the structural report did not include, showing moderate concordance among RNA, WSI, and WXS and lower concordance with CT. The two reports are complementary and jointly describe a partition whose boundary is modest in both fused and native geometries.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 versus the rest of the partition, the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a coherent, multi-pathway phenotype. The strongest signal is up-enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain genes, accompanied by up-enrichment of reactive oxygen species pathway (NES 1.82, FDR 0.0022), fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, and MTORC1 signaling. A second coherent axis is immune/inflammatory: interferon-gamma response (NES 1.72, FDR 0.0015), allograft rejection (NES 1.78, FDR 0.0018), interferon-alpha response (NES 1.74, FDR 0.0022), complement, IL6-JAK-STAT3, inflammatory response, and apoptosis are all up-enriched with low FDR, sharing many HLA, interferon-stimulated, and cytokine leading-edge genes. A third axis is proliferative: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, MYC targets V1/V2, and glycolysis are up-enriched. Down-enriched pathways include UV response DN (NES -1.86, FDR 0.0065), TGF-beta signaling, WNT beta-catenin signaling, and Hedgehog signaling. The direction and magnitude of these results indicate that K2_C0001 is characterized by a metabolically active, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative expression program relative to the rest of the partition. Because this is a K=2 contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0002-versus-rest result is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent biological confirmation. The FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity adjustments and do not by themselves establish biological importance.
biological_support.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics for this partition described comparable internal cohesion of the two sets and a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry, with partition-level eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. That report did not include RNA pathway measurements, so the present enrichment results are complementary rather than directly comparable: they add a biological-phenotype description of K2_C0001 that the structural report could not provide. The reciprocal K2_C0002 report in this round is the other side of the same two-group contrast and should be read together with this one, not as independent confirmation.
limitations: The analysis is a single set-versus-rest contrast in a K=2 partition; the reciprocal K2_C0002 result is not an independent biological confirmation.

These are correspondence analyses, not independent validation, and both taxonomies overlap the RNA discovery view. The clinical associations indicate that the partition is not independent of clinical stratification, but the effect sizes are modest and the clinical labels are not discovery features.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant associations with candidate membership after BH correction within their respective test families. Tissue source site has the largest categorical association (Cramer's V 0.434, q=0.009), followed by CT phase (V 0.316, q=0.028) and CT scanner model (V 0.310, q=0.028). Among continuous acquisition factors, CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.066, q=0.026) and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.048, q=0.028) are significantly associated, while CT pixel spacing (q=0.092) and study year (q=0.216) are not. CT manufacturer (q=0.224) and CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.112) are also not significant. The pattern indicates that site and some CT acquisition characteristics are unevenly distributed across the two candidate sets, which could plausibly contribute to the observed partition geometry. However, these are associations, not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors may also reflect genuine clinical or biological differences between the patient groups. The nonsignificant results do not establish absence of confounding, and the categorical and continuous test families receive separate multiplicity corrections.

The present confounder associations are relevant to that structural picture because uneven site and CT acquisition distributions could contribute to the weak boundary, but the structural report did not measure technical factors, so the two reports are complementary rather than directly comparable. No prior confounder report is available for this partition.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001 versus the rest of the partition, the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a coherent, multi-pathway phenotype. The strongest signal is up-enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (NES 2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain genes, accompanied by up-enrichment of reactive oxygen species pathway (NES 1.82, FDR 0.0022), fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, and MTORC1 signaling. A second coherent axis is immune/inflammatory: interferon-gamma response (NES 1.72, FDR 0.0015), allograft rejection (NES 1.78, FDR 0.0018), interferon-alpha response (NES 1.74, FDR 0.0022), complement, IL6-JAK-STAT3, inflammatory response, and apoptosis are all up-enriched with low FDR, sharing many HLA, interferon-stimulated, and cytokine leading-edge genes. A third axis is proliferative: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, MYC targets V1/V2, and glycolysis are up-enriched. Down-enriched pathways include UV response DN (NES -1.86, FDR 0.0065), TGF-beta signaling, WNT beta-catenin signaling, and Hedgehog signaling. The direction and magnitude of these results indicate that K2_C0001 is characterized by a metabolically active, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative expression program relative to the rest of the partition. Because this is a K=2 contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0002-versus-rest result is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent biological confirmation. The FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity adjustments and do not by themselves establish biological importance.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics for this partition described comparable internal cohesion of the two sets and a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry, with partition-level eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. That report did not include RNA pathway measurements, so the present enrichment results are complementary rather than directly comparable: they add a biological-phenotype description of K2_C0001 that the structural report could not provide. The reciprocal K2_C0002 report in this round is the other side of the same two-group contrast and should be read together with this one, not as independent confirmation.
limitations: The analysis is a single set-versus-rest contrast in a K=2 partition; the reciprocal K2_C0002 result is not an independent biological confirmation.
GSEA FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity adjustments and do not establish biological importance or causality.
The ranking uses the unshrunken PyDESeq2 Wald statistic from raw integer counts; results depend on that ranking method and on the finite set of 19,449 ranked genes.
Leading-edge gene overlap across pathways (e.g., interferon, allograft rejection, inflammatory response) means the pathway signals are not fully independent of one another.
No mutation-level or protein-level measurements are included here, so the phenotype is described at the RNA pathway level only.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant associations with candidate membership after BH correction within their respective test families. Tissue source site has the largest categorical association (Cramer's V 0.434, q=0.009), followed by CT phase (V 0.316, q=0.028) and CT scanner model (V 0.310, q=0.028). Among continuous acquisition factors, CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.066, q=0.026) and CT z-spacing (epsilon-squared 0.048, q=0.028) are significantly associated, while CT pixel spacing (q=0.092) and study year (q=0.216) are not. CT manufacturer (q=0.224) and CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.112) are also not significant. The pattern indicates that site and some CT acquisition characteristics are unevenly distributed across the two candidate sets, which could plausibly contribute to the observed partition geometry. However, these are associations, not proof of technical artifact or causation; the significant factors may also reflect genuine clinical or biological differences between the patient groups. The nonsignificant results do not establish absence of confounding, and the categorical and continuous test families receive separate multiplicity corrections.

reports.dimension_interpretation: The current K2_C0001/K2_C0002 labels separate only weakly in each modality's native distance geometry: RNA silhouette 0.079, WXS 0.091, WSI 0.050, and CT 0.013. The CT silhouette is near zero, indicating essentially no separation of the current labels in CT distance space, while the other three modalities show small positive separation. Global patient-geometry similarity (GRV) is highest between WSI and RNA (0.198, permutation p=0.001), followed by CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001) and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001); these pairs share more global patient geometry than expected under exchangeable correspondence. CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096) show lower GRV with nonsignificant permutation p-values. The pattern indicates that the four views are not uniformly concordant: the RNA, WSI, and WXS views share moderate global geometry with each other, while CT is the least concordant with the molecular views. Importantly, high GRV does not establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and low GRV can reflect complementary information rather than a faulty modality. The weak native-distance silhouettes indicate that the current pair boundary is not sharply expressed in any single view, consistent with the weakly expressed boundary described in the prior structural report.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics described comparable internal cohesion of the two sets and a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry, with partition-level eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The GRV results add a cross-view geometry comparison that the structural report did not include, showing moderate concordance among RNA, WSI, and WXS and lower concordance with CT. The two reports are complementary and jointly describe a partition whose boundary is modest in both fused and native geometries.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic evaluates whether the current two-set membership is coherently represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The two sets are of comparable size (55 and 48) and show nearly identical mean within-set affinity (0.00929 and 0.00936), indicating similar internal cohesion. The between-set affinity (0.00902) is only slightly lower than either within-set value, so the current pair boundary is weakly expressed in fused affinity terms rather than sharply separated. The eigengap profiles for both sets are dominated by the k=1 resolution (leading gaps 0.328 and 0.301), with all higher-resolution gaps falling to the 10^-3 to 10^-4 range; the screening therefore resolves to candidate_k=1 for both sets. Taken together, the measurements describe a partition whose two memberships are internally comparable and whose boundary is modest in fused geometry, while the partition-level screening does not surface a dominant internal subdivision signal. These are structural descriptions of the current partition, not conclusions about whether the partition should be retained, split, or merged.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002 versus the rest of the partition, the ranked enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a phenotype that is largely the mirror image of the K2_C0001 result. The strongest signal is down-enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.29, FDR 0.001), with a leading edge of mitochondrial respiratory-chain genes, accompanied by down-enrichment of reactive oxygen species pathway (NES -1.85, FDR 0.0018), MTORC1 signaling, fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis, and glycolysis. Immune/inflammatory pathways are also down-enriched: allograft rejection (NES -1.79, FDR 0.0018), interferon-gamma response (NES -1.72, FDR 0.0022), interferon-alpha response (NES -1.74, FDR 0.0022), complement, IL6-JAK-STAT3, inflammatory response, and apoptosis. Proliferative pathways are down-enriched: DNA repair, E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, MYC targets V1/V2, and estrogen response late. Up-enriched pathways include UV response DN (NES 1.84, FDR 0.0063), TGF-beta signaling, Hedgehog signaling, and WNT beta-catenin signaling. The direction and magnitude of these results indicate that K2_C0002 is characterized by lower oxidative-phosphorylation, immune/inflammatory, and proliferative expression programs relative to the rest of the partition, with relative up-enrichment of TGF-beta, Hedgehog, and WNT signaling. Because this is a K=2 contrast, the reciprocal K2_C0001-versus-rest result is the same two-group contrast viewed from the other side, not an independent biological confirmation. The FDR values are pathway-level multiplicity adjustments and do not by themselves establish biological importance.

The reciprocal K2_C0001 report in this round is the other side of the same two-group contrast and should be read together with this one, not as independent confirmation.

reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic evaluates whether the current two-set membership is coherently represented in the fused four-view patient geometry. The two sets are of comparable size (55 and 48) and show nearly identical mean within-set affinity (0.00929 and 0.00936), indicating similar internal cohesion. The between-set affinity (0.00902) is only slightly lower than either within-set value, so the current pair boundary is weakly expressed in fused affinity terms rather than sharply separated. The eigengap profiles for both sets are dominated by the k=1 resolution (leading gaps 0.328 and 0.301), with all higher-resolution gaps falling to the 10^-3 to 10^-4 range; the screening therefore resolves to candidate_k=1 for both sets. Taken together, the measurements describe a partition whose two memberships are internally comparable and whose boundary is modest in fused geometry, while the partition-level screening does not surface a dominant internal subdivision signal. These are structural descriptions of the current partition, not conclusions about whether the partition should be retained, split, or merged.

reports.dimension_interpretation: The current K2_C0001/K2_C0002 labels separate only weakly in each modality's native distance geometry: RNA silhouette 0.079, WXS 0.091, WSI 0.050, and CT 0.013. The CT silhouette is near zero, indicating essentially no separation of the current labels in CT distance space, while the other three modalities show small positive separation. Global patient-geometry similarity (GRV) is highest between WSI and RNA (0.198, permutation p=0.001), followed by CT-WSI (0.167, p=0.001) and RNA-WXS (0.145, p=0.001); these pairs share more global patient geometry than expected under exchangeable correspondence. CT-WXS (0.103, p=0.218), CT-RNA (0.092, p=0.071), and WSI-WXS (0.092, p=0.096) show lower GRV with nonsignificant permutation p-values. The pattern indicates that the four views are not uniformly concordant: the RNA, WSI, and WXS views share moderate global geometry with each other, while CT is the least concordant with the molecular views. Importantly, high GRV does not establish that two views support the same candidate boundary, and low GRV can reflect complementary information rather than a faulty modality. The weak native-distance silhouettes indicate that the current pair boundary is not sharply expressed in any single view, consistent with the weakly expressed boundary described in the prior structural report.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics described comparable internal cohesion of the two sets and a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry, with partition-level eigengap screening dominated by the single-cluster resolution. The present native-distance silhouettes are consistent with that picture: the current labels separate only weakly in each single-view geometry, and the CT view shows essentially no separation. The GRV results add a cross-view geometry comparison that the structural report did not include, showing moderate concordance among RNA, WSI, and WXS and lower concordance with CT. The two reports are complementary and jointly describe a partition whose boundary is modest in both fused and native geometries.
limitations: GRV describes similarity between patient-level modality geometries, not direct raw-feature similarity, biological agreement, or independent validation.
High GRV does not establish that two views support the same candidate boundary; low GRV can reflect complementary information.
The tool does not recluster patients; the silhouettes describe alignment of the existing candidate labels only.
For K=2, the two set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal descriptions of the same two-group partition and are not independent confirmations.
Permutation p-values test exchangeability of patient correspondence and are not action thresholds; bootstrap intervals describe paired patient-resampling uncertainty.

reports.dimension_interpretation: The candidate partition shows statistically significant but modest associations with clinical stratification: grade (Cramer's V 0.219, p=0.032), stage (V 0.273, p=0.018), T stage (V 0.247, p=0.021), and M stage (V 0.202, p=0.026). The direction of the associations is that K2_C0001 contains more advanced-stage and higher-grade patients (more stage III/IV, T3, G4, and M1), while K2_C0002 contains more early-stage and lower-grade patients. The reciprocal M0/M1 Fisher tests give the same p-value (0.041), reflecting that they are two views of the same two-group contrast. For established molecular taxonomies, agreement is low: TCGA m1-m4 (AMI 0.133, ARI 0.146) and ClearCode34 (AMI 0.181, ARI 0.240). The contingency tables show that TCGA m1 and ClearCode34 ccA are concentrated in K2_C0002, while TCGA m3/m4 and ClearCode34 ccB are more frequent in K2_C0001. These are correspondence analyses, not independent validation, and both taxonomies overlap the RNA discovery view. The clinical associations indicate that the partition is not independent of clinical stratification, but the effect sizes are modest and the clinical labels are not discovery features.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report on structural diagnostics described a weakly expressed boundary in fused affinity geometry. The present clinical and taxonomy associations add a known-label context: the partition aligns modestly with clinical stage and grade and weakly with established expression-derived taxonomies. This is complementary to the structural report, which did not measure clinical or taxonomy correspondence. The RNA pathway enrichment reports in this round describe a metabolic/immune/proliferative phenotype for K2_C0001 and the mirror image for K2_C0002; the taxonomy correspondence is consistent with the partition capturing some known biological variation, but it is not independent validation because the taxonomies overlap the RNA discovery view.
limitations: TCGA m1-m4 and ClearCode34 overlap the RNA discovery view; this is taxonomy correspondence, not independent validation.
Clinical associations are modest in magnitude and do not establish clinical utility or prognosis.
M stage has 5 missing values, so its analysis uses 98 patients rather than 103.
The reciprocal M0/M1 Fisher tests are not independent confirmations.
Clinical labels are not discovery features and their association with the partition does not establish that the partition is clinically meaningful.
